## Goal

Convert the measured window (sibling measurement item) into the AC3 closure verdict for the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I, keep the parent-AC4 evidence trail current, and re-point the ownership link now that the scheduler epic has landed without removing the residual.

## Context

- **AC1 is already recorded.** The parent AC4 re-scope comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D (2026-10-25T20:39) references this item and the 12 user-traffic events / 7.4 h measurement with the audit split. Re-confirm it against the fresh window.
- **AC2's edge is mechanically satisfied but stale.** The depends-on edge to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG exists and the epic is completed, yet the residual survived it. At intake the live fix owner was recorded as LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (predicted-warmth / `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owned the fix's own post-deploy measurement. **Updated at the verdict (2026-10-30):** both are terminal (Option D live from the 2026-10-29T00:10:19Z restart; F5's post-deploy window measured under LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE) and the residual survived them — 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions in the 24 h post-deploy window. The live mechanism owner is now **LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2** (abandoned-prefill backlog); see *Relationships* below.
- **AC4's rollback note is in the description.** Re-affirm it with the fresh window's numbers.

## Scope

**In:** the AC3 verdict; the AC3(b) producer re-scope proposal when path (a) fails; evidence, link and rollback recording on this item and in a parent-AC4 comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D; description updates limited to the Ownership / Relationships / Key Files lines that the measurements proved stale.

**Out:** any code change; any change to parent AC4 text or thresholds without explicit producer approval (AC3(b)); measurement work (the sibling measurement item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Parent AC1 (Evidence recorded).** "**AC1 — Evidence recorded.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is referenced from the parent AC4 comment." — re-confirmed with the post-occupancy-fix window and referenced from a parent AC4 comment.
- **AC2 — Parent AC2 (Link established).** "**AC2 — Link established.** A related edge points to LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG so the producer can fold this into the scheduler scope (or explicitly re-scope parent AC4 to exclude audit traffic / warm-HOL)." — recorded as satisfied (depends-on edge present; epic completed 2026-10-25T23:44Z).
- **AC2b — Successor link recorded.** Because the residual survived the scheduler epic, the live fix owner LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (with its F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD) is recorded as the successor link in this item's description and a related-to comment — not as a `wl dep add` edge, which would set this item `blocked` before its own verdict work can run — and the superseded occupancy hypothesis is stated explicitly.
- **AC3 — Parent AC3 (Closure).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — a written verdict records which path applies: either (a) is certified from the measurement window, or (a) fails and an AC3(b) re-scope proposal (recommended user-traffic threshold, rationale and measurement plan) is put to the producer with `wl reviewed LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I true`. No parent AC4 text, threshold or AC is changed without an explicit producer reply recorded on this item; the item closes only on the matching condition.
- **AC4 — Parent AC4 (Rollback note).** "**AC4 — Rollback note.** No rollback recommended: the budget change is working (−88 % deadline rate, 0 over-budget admissions, −83 % wasted tokens); rolling back restores the thrash without touching this residual." — re-affirmed with the fresh window's numbers and recorded on this item and in the parent AC4 comment.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`EVICTION_REASONS`, `log_local_eviction`) — the closed reason vocabulary the verdict reports against
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (`ProjectedWait`, `evaluate_admission`) — the admission maths the rollback note refers to
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` — the window evidence the verdict cites
- `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` — the analyser that produces every figure the verdict cites (same classifier as the parent AC4 measurement)
- `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual.md` and `docs/dev/prefill-deadline-residual-2026-10-29.json` — the recorded report and per-event dataset (commit `56d853be`)

## Relationships (successor links, recorded 2026-10-30 — AC2b)

The residual survived the scheduler epic **and** the Option D fix, so the fix ownership is re-pointed here. Recorded as this description plus a related-to comment, deliberately **not** as a `wl dep add` edge: a dependency on a non-terminal item would set this verdict item `blocked` before its own recording work can run.

- **Superseded fix owner:** LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D `measured_cache_deficit` early abort, F4 `1908f431`) with F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD and its post-deploy delegate LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE — all terminal; their own ≥24 h post-deploy window still shows 47 user-class `prefill_deadline` evictions.
- **Live mechanism owner (successor):** LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 — an early-released dispatch keeps prefilling in `llama-server` and starves the next dispatch (26 % of the day's prefill compute thrown away; 58 of the 60 measured events started inside an abandoned-prefill window). Discovered from the measurement item LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O.
- **Predecessor evidence:** LP-0MVRMOT0N005136O (measured window, `completed` — this item's blocker, satisfied).
- **Parent-AC4 owner:** LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D — its AC4 carries the residual clause; the refreshed evidence comment was posted there with this verdict.
- **Superseded hypothesis, stated explicitly:** second-slot head-of-line blocking (a warm prompt blocked behind another session's prefill) is **superseded** — it explains 9 of 60 events (15 %), and none of those 9 had another session's lease extended inside its window. The dominant cause (43 of 60, 72 %) is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: priced at ~95 % cached (`p50` priced cached ratio 0.946), zero backend prefill progress for the whole 120 s lease, and a retry that re-enters at the same price — kept alive by the abandoned-prefill backlog.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — producer availability.** AC3(b) needs an explicit producer reply; if none arrives the item stays open with the question recorded (AC3).
- **Risk — stale-link confusion.** Recording the successor link as a `wl dep add` edge would set this item `blocked`; the description/comment form in AC2b preserves dispatchability at the cost of a softer link.
- **Risk — re-scope fatigue.** The parent AC4 has already been re-scoped once (2026-10-25); the AC3(b) proposal must state why a further re-scope is warranted rather than assuming it.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the sibling measurement item. The closure certification also needs LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (fix) and its F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (post-deploy measurement) to be terminal; this is recorded as a stated prerequisite rather than a `wl dep add` edge so the recording work remains dispatchable.

## Deliverables

A verdict comment on this item (path (a) certified, or (a)-fails plus the AC3(b) proposal), the parent-AC4 evidence comment on LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D, and the re-affirmed rollback note.

data.description:
## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

## Relationship to LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R

Spun out of `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (contention-queue sweep) as a **top-level,
standalone measurement item** on 2026-10-31 (operator decision), so the sweep
parent can reach `in_review` at code-complete while this scheduled observation
runs on its own calendar. Recorded as `discovered-from:LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R`;
the parent is no longer a dependency. The sweep's three implementation
children are already on `dev`: `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` (report + ≥ 24 h pre-flip
baseline, `65621b8b`), `LP-0MVT1146V007WXA4` (30 s / depth 2, `6a6e2f38`),
`LP-0MVT114HU009UNML` (docs as straggler net, `47f973e0`).

## Earliest run date

**Earliest run: 2026-11-07** — i.e. restart date + 7 days. The window starts
only once the swept config is live (dev→main release, then a quiet-window proxy
restart that loads 30 s / depth 2). If the release/restart lands later than
2026-10-31, this date moves with it: the item is runnable on restart date + 7
days, and never earlier than ≥ 1 000 post-flip queue events (AC5 forbids a
verdict from partial data).

Follow-up split out of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 intake answer Q1 (scope = guard-only, `B`). Attribution of individual router-responder `GET /slots ... 400` events is currently impossible from `llama-server.log` because llama.cpp's router access line omits the query string (`srv log_server_r: done request: GET /slots 127.0.0.1 400` is identical with and without `?model=`, verified empirically 2026-10-29).

## Problem

`_query_slots_detail` and `_query_slots_progress` (`proxy/proxy/observability.py:695`/`:773`) swallow non-200 responses silently — no failure metric, debug-level logging only — so a 400 on those paths is invisible in `/metrics` and `proxy.log`. - Record `llama_slots_query_failures_total{reason="http_400"}` (and other non-200 reasons) from the detail/progress query paths, aligned with the existing `_query_slots` precedent.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want each `slot_ratio_seed` line to carry the snapshot path it
resolved (or the candidate paths it tried) and whether the sidecar was present,
so the remaining per-session cause of `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot` is
attributable from logs instead of inferred from code inspection.

## Why (evidence)

The verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md)
proved from 4,488 decisions that the seed path always fails at the lookup
(`missing_sidecar` 75.8 %, `missing_snapshot` 24.2 %; `found`, `expired`,
`prefix_mismatch` all 0). It identified two provable writer-side gaps (the
eviction save path writes no sidecar; the request path skips the sidecar when no
usage block was measured) but could not split the 31 affected sessions between
them, because `missing_sidecar` records `stored_messages=0` by design and logs
neither the resolved `slot_<session>.bin` path nor the sidecar path.

## Scope

**In scope:** one extra field on the existing INFO line (behaviour-neutral) plus
tests/docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision, `prefix_matches`,
the TTL, or the sidecar format (those belong to LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).

1. In `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, extend `log_seed_outcome()` with an
   optional `slot=<basename>` field (basename only — no absolute paths in logs)

2. Cover every outcome branch in `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`.
3. Document the extra field in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

- Every `slot_ratio_seed` line names the resolved snapshot basename (or the

## Goal

Update the two client-facing refusal strings that still describe the pre-deferral
`local-only` semantics, so the remedy the proxy advertises matches the shipped
`local-preferred` contract documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## What is stale

- `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, the `suggested_action` for
  `retryable: false`): still ends with "or send X-Local-Preference: prefer-local to
  allow a remote fallback". After LP-0MVSHXTLS000VMLE a `too_large` `local-preferred`
  request is already promoted to the remote tiers automatically, so that clause is
  redundant for a pin-local client and misleading for a `prefer-local` one (which
  falls through without any preference change). The compaction half (compact to
  `budget_tokens` and resend) is correct and should stay.
- The deferral 429 body `detail` in `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`: still
  reads "X-Local-Preference: local-only forbids remote fallback" — a deprecated
  spelling, and a description that contradicts the retryable deferral the same
  response now carries.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 `_COMPACTION_GUIDANCE` names the compaction remedy and the token target, and
  no longer tells the client to change its preference to reach a remote tier.
- AC2 The deferral 429 `detail` names `local-preferred` (or no preference value at
  all) and describes the deferral rather than an unconditional refusal.
- AC3 The strings stay consistent with `proxy/docs/routing.md`'s per-reason retry
  contract (`suggested_action`, AC2 of LP-0MVSHXU8E004BL57) — a doc-contract or
  unit test pins the wording/remedy so it cannot drift again.
- AC4 Full suite green at the dev-push gate.

## Constraints

- Strings only: no routing, timing or refusal-shape behaviour change.
- Any test that pins the current wording moves with the string in the same commit.

## Problem

`proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py::TestCitationsStillResolve` has produced a
**critical `test-failure` work item four times in two days**:

| Item | Created | Cited symbol that drifted |
|---|---|---|
| LP-0MVS0CU4V006FLLC | 2026-10-28 | `router.py::_get_local_max_concurrent_queries` 150 → 152, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` call site 1264 → 1304 |
| LP-0MVREECR9009UN78 | 2026-10-28 | `router.py` citations again |
| LP-0MVSFCP59004XXCG | 2026-10-28 | `router_helpers.py` 2697 → 2764, 2370 → 2430 |
| LP-0MVTHCT8W003VAGE | 2026-10-29 | `router_helpers.py` 2430 → 2631, 2764 → 2965 |

Each item's only change is renumbering `file:line` citations in
`docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` and the matching
`CITATIONS` tuples in the test. No cited behaviour changed in any of the four
occurrences — only line numbers moved.

## Why it keeps happening

The test pins **absolute line numbers** for 36 citations and tolerates
`CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE = 60` lines of drift. Every unrelated commit inside
`proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
(a 6,415-line module that grows fastest of the three) shifts the cited symbols.
Headroom is already thin as of 2026-10-29: `proxy/proxy/router.py:152`
(`def _get_local_max_concurrent_queries`) sits at **drift 55 of 60** — roughly five
inserted lines above it in `router.py` reddens the tree again. The `provider.py`
citations sit at a uniform drift of 16.

Verification (plan session 2026-10-29, read-only): all 36 citations resolve; max
drift 55 (`router.py:152`), next 25 (`provider.py:6127`), next 16 (`provider.py` ×6).

## Options (producer to choose — do not pre-empt)

- **A. Symbol-anchored citations (recommended).** The doc cites `file` + symbol
  (e.g. `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`effective_per_slot_threshold`)) without a line
  number, and the test asserts the symbol exists in that file (and, where useful,
  that the occurrence is unique / inside the expected enclosing definition). A move
  inside a file can no longer fail the suite; removal or rename still does.
- **B. Generated citation index.** Keep line numbers but stop hand-maintaining them:
  a small script derives each cited line from the symbol and rewrites the doc block;
  the test (or a check step) runs the generator and fails only if the committed
  block differs from regenerated output — a one-command fix instead of a new
  critical work item.
- **C. Raise/parameterise tolerance.** Cheapest, but knowingly keeps the treadmill;
  it also weakens the check (a symbol that genuinely moves far away is no longer
  caught). Acceptable only as a stopgap.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 The sizing-doc citation check can no longer fail solely because a cited symbol
  moved *within* its file: a test moves a synthetic symbol down a synthetic source by
  more than the current tolerance and asserts the check still passes.
- AC2 The check still fails when a cited symbol is removed or renamed in its file
  (guard test, mirroring the existing `test_missing_symbol_is_reported`).
- AC3 All existing citations are migrated to the chosen scheme, in the same commit as
  the scheme change (`docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` +
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py`), with no cited behaviour dropped.
- AC4 The doc remains readable by an operator: each citation still names a file and a
  symbol precise enough to locate the behaviour by search (no bare "see provider.py").
- AC5 The decision (option A/B/C with rationale) is recorded on this item, including
  what happens to `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`.
- AC6 Full project test suite passes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change; docs + test only.
- Do not weaken the check into a no-op — AC1/AC2 must both hold.
- The test's doc-table fidelity assertions (`TestProductionGeometry`,
  `TestDocTableFidelity`) are out of scope and must stay green.

## Key Files (verified 2026-10-29)

- `proxy/tests/test_slot_pool_sizing_doc.py` — `CITATION_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`,
  `_resolve_citation()`, `TestCitationsStillResolve.CITATIONS`, `TestCitationDriftGuard`.
- `docs/dev/slot-snapshot-pool-sizing-LP-0MVN3KPEC007WWL5.md` — §1 nine-behaviour table
  (rows 1–9 carry the 36 citations).
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/session.py`, `proxy/proxy/handlers.py`, `proxy/proxy/capacity_admission.py`,
  `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`, `start-llama.sh`,
  `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh` — cited sources (read-only for this item).

## Problem

The automated code-quality review (epic LP-0MVTJXBKO00843I8, tag `Refactor`) filed three work items — one CRITICAL, one HIGH, one MEDIUM — against `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`, a **gitignored, untracked** local analysis scratch script:

- LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (critical, F401 unused `sys`)
- LP-0MVTJXC1D003NS8F (high, E401 multiple imports on one line)
- LP-0MVTJXCCL008DOEO (medium, I001 unsorted import block)

`.worklog/` is excluded by `.gitignore` (rule `.worklog/`, confirmed with `git check-ignore -v`), and `ruff` itself honours `.gitignore` on directory recursion. Findings on untracked scratch files cannot be remediated by a commit, so each becomes a verification-only no-op item — scheduling noise, and a CRITICAL-tagged one competes with real defects in `wl next`.

## Root cause

The review scan enumerates files by explicit path (or walks the tree without honouring `.gitignore`), so gitignored paths enter the lint scope.

## Proposed fix

- Scope the scan to git-tracked files (`git ls-files`), or add explicit exclusions for gitignored paths / `.worklog/`.
- Optionally suppress findings whose file is untracked (no committable remediation path exists).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The code-quality review emits no findings for files excluded by `.gitignore` (verified by a scan covering `.worklog/analysis/` and observing no findings for it).
- [ ] A regression check covers the scan scope (test or documented scope assertion).
- [ ] No severity inflation: a finding on a gitignored path is either not filed, or filed at `low` with an explicit "untracked scratch file" note.

## Provenance

Discovered while implementing LP-0MVTJXCN7000V3SA (no-op verification close of the F401 finding for the same gitignored file).

# Verify the post-cancel release-lag fix: did the draining-slot annotation remove the residual saturated-without-live-work polls?

Standalone verification of the fix delivered by **LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM**
("Annotate the post-cancel release lag so a draining slot is never reported
saturated"). Formerly the AC5 child of that item; promoted to a top-level item
so the fixing item can be completed/in_review and this measurement can run on
its own schedule, against a real post-deploy night.

## Why this item exists

The fix (landed on `dev`) makes the proxy annotate a slot it is still draining
after abandoning the work, so such a slot reads `abandoned_busy` instead of
`saturated`. The code change is verified by deterministic tests. **This item
answers the operational question the fix was written for:** over a comparable
night of real traffic with the fix deployed, are there still
`capacity_hint=saturated` polls with `local_in_flight_requests=0` and fresh slot
detail — and is any residual attributable?

Baselines to compare against (both measured with the narrower four-reason
abandonment set; the widened set now includes `measured_cache_deficit`, so
before/after is read knowingly):

| Baseline | Window | `saturated`-without-live-work polls |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-fix (AC1) | 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00 | 247 polls / 2.12 % |
| Post-AC1 residual (AC4) | 2026-10-29 20:00 → 2026-10-30 07:00 | 12 polls / 0.11 % (5 unattributable) |

## Required summary (the deliverable)

The verdict must lead with an unambiguous statement a producer can act on,
without reading the raw artifacts:

1. **Was the expected improvement achieved?** An explicit
   `EXPECTED IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVED: YES / NO / INCONCLUSIVE` line, with the
   measured count and rate of `saturated`-without-live-work polls beside the
   12-poll / 0.11 % residual baseline and the 247-poll / 2.12 % pre-fix
   baseline, and the change stated as an absolute delta and as a factor.
2. **Is the fix visibly working, not merely absent?** The `abandoned_busy`
   poll count and rate, so the result reads as a *shift* from `saturated` to
   `abandoned_busy` rather than a "nothing happened" zero. If `abandoned_busy`
   is also 0, say so explicitly and state what that implies (either no
   abandonment occurred in the window, or the annotation did not fire).
3. **Is every residual accounted for?** `ATTRIBUTION: n rows, m attributed,
   k unattributable`, with any unattributed poll's timestamp, its registry
   scope (`slot` / `endpoint` / none) and the nearest abandonment or restart
   event. An unattributable residual is a finding, not a rounding error.
4. **Is additional work recommended?** An explicit
   `ADDITIONAL WORK RECOMMENDED: YES (items …) / NO` line — naming concrete
   work items or stating "none, the acceptance target is met".
5. **Provenance sufficient to trust the numbers:** window bounds (local),
   `--window-closed`, deployed commit, proxy process start time, coverage
   verdict (`covered=true`, no gaps), and the verbatim measurement command.
   A proxy restart or deploy *inside* the window makes the window mixed-build:
   say so and re-measure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **A clear achieved/not-achieved verdict.** The report opens with
  `EXPECTED IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVED: <YES|NO|INCONCLUSIVE>` plus the measured
  count and rate of `saturated`-without-live-work polls, compared against both
  baselines above (the fix target is **0** polls).
- **The improvement is visible as a shift.** `abandoned_busy` polls are
  reported separately with count and rate, and their presence/absence is
  interpreted (an all-zero window must say why).
- **Every residual is attributed or declared unattributable** row by row
  (registry scope present? endpoint-wide? nearest abandonment reason; restart
  attributable), with the lookback window stated.
- **An explicit recommendation.** `ADDITIONAL WORK RECOMMENDED: <YES (with
  work-item ids) | NO>` — no report is complete without it.
- **Comparable window.** The measured span is a full night of the same length
  as the baselines (20:00 → 07:00 local), asserted closed, and lies entirely
  after the deployed proxy's process start time.
- **Reproducible.** The verbatim command, the tool version/behaviour notes
  (including the widened abandonment-reason set), and the artifact paths are
  stated; artifacts are persisted under
  `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/` (`measurement.json`,
  `measurement.txt`, per-poll CSV,
  `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`, `deployment.txt`,
  `verdict.txt`).
- **Read-only.** The measurement never restarts, kills or reconfigures the
  proxy, and never changes proxy behaviour to obtain evidence.
- **Verdict recorded** as a comment on this item, with a short pointer comment
  on LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM for traceability.

## Minimal implementation

The scheduled runner already does the measurement and posts the numbers:
`~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/run_measurement.sh`
(one-shot cron block `begin/end-night-remeasure-LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1`, firing
2026-11-02 07:10 local, 10 minutes after the window closes). The remaining work

data.description:
**Discovered while producing the AC4 post-change record** (`LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN`; record: `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md`). **Not a release blocker**: the literal parent AC4 bar (< 85 %) and the no-new-eviction clause both hold. This item tracks the *stricter* working-baseline regression that the same record reports.

## Finding (committed harness, same 24 h basis, same code path per window)

Post-change window `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `2026-10-30 00:10:18` UTC (deploy `52085f09`) vs pre-change `2026-10-27 19:00` → `2026-10-28 19:00`.

- Abandoned-queue-wait share: **36.9 % (24/65) → 60.7 % (314/517)**.
- Abandoned waits per hour: **1.0 /h → 13.1 /h**; queued local waits per hour **2.7 /h → 21.5 /h**.
- Admits/hour **17.6 → 53.3** (×3.0), rejects/hour **164.8 → 114.3** (×0.69) — the queue denominator grew with traffic, but the *share* also grew in four of five bands (`<8k` 35.1→49.5, `8k-20k` 50.0→64.6, `20k-32k` 0→78.8, `32k-64k` 0→91.1).
- Evictions are **not** the cause: `local_eviction_after_acceptance` 392 (16.3 /h) vs 463 (19.3 /h) pre-change, all five reason classes pre-existing.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator I want to understand why the abandoned-queue-wait share rose after the contended-pricing fix — despite the contended bucket and the occupant-remaining rebase provably serving — so that queue-budget/ETA behaviour under the new (~3×) local admission volume is correct rather than merely below the historical 85 % bar.

## Open questions for intake

- Is the rise a *fundamental* consequence of admitting ~3× more local dispatches (more marginal admits queue, then hit the 60 s `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget), i.e. the admission guard is now too **permissive** rather than too optimistic?
- Why does band `32k-64k` show 45 queued waits and 41 abandoned (91.1 %) with **zero** admits — where do those queued waits come from if every admission in that band was rejected?
- Should the working baseline be recomputed on a diurnally matched window (`00:10`→`00:10` pre-change) before calling this a regression? Both windows are exactly 24 h, so per-hour rates are comparable, but the mix is not identical.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-postchange.md` / `.json` (source numbers; reproducible)
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py --since "2026-10-29 00:10:18" --until "2026-10-30 00:10:18" --json` (eviction counters included)
- Parent epic: `LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3`; AC4 record carrier: `LP-0MVTKTOVI006ZONN`


## Measured refinement (planning session, 2026-10-30)

The three intake questions are answered below with numbers reproducible from
`/var/log/llama-proxy` using the committed harness vocabulary. Two of the
answers change the framing of this item before any behaviour change is
planned.

### 1. The baseline window is diurnally mismatched — most of the headline is mix

The fix was deployed at `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC (`52085f09`), so
`2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC is a **fully pre-change-code**
24 h window that is diurnally matched to the post-change window:

| Window (24 h) | Code | Enqueued waits | Abandoned | Share | Admits | Rejects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | pre | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 423 | 3 954 |
| `10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` | pre | 136 | 71 | **52.6 %** | 576 | 4 078 |
| `10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` | `52085f09` | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 1 278 | 2 742 |

So the like-for-like change is **52.6 % → 60.7 % (+8.1 points)**; the
36.9 % → 52.6 % step is diurnal mix (the 19:00→19:00 window is quieter), not
the contended-pricing change. This answers open question 3: yes, the baseline
must be recomputed diurnally, and it is a measurement slice of its own
(`LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK`).

### 2. Per-band numbers are contaminated by a harness attribution defect

`build_report()`'s `band_for_queue()` bands a queue wait by the session's
nearest *preceding* admission and, when none precedes, falls back to
`(preceding or candidates)[-1:]` — the session's latest admission, **even one
hours after the queue event**. That is the origin of the phantom `32k-64k` row
(45 queued waits / 41 abandoned / **0 admits**): those waits belong to sessions
whose only admission evidence is a later `prefill_budget_exceeded` reject.
Verified example: session `herdr-1793285755-177798-1619` abandons at
`14:56:57` and its only admission line is a 35 077-token reject at `15:01:35`
(4 m 38 s later). The **totals are unaffected** (banding does not change them),
but every per-band claim — including "the share grew in four of five bands" —
is untrustworthy until fixed (`LP-0MVV29WR0009DY1A`). This answers open
question 2: those waits are an attribution artefact, to be proven per-wait by
`LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5`.

### 3. Every abandonment is a budget expiry, not a depth refusal

`queued_duration >= 55 s` for **314/314** post-change and **71/71** pre-change
diurnal abandonments; depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur. The 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth` (8). Today that distinction is inferred from the
duration rather than logged (`LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL`).

### 4. Two entry paths, one of them a retry without priority

| Window (24 h) | lease-active waits / abandoned | concurrency-limit waits / abandoned |
|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | 48 / 20 = 41.7 % | 17 / 4 = 23.5 % |
| `10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` | 107 / 57 = 53.3 % | 28 / 14 = 50.0 % |
| `10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` | 368 / 225 = 61.1 % | 149 / 89 = 59.7 % |

225 of 314 post-change abandonments (71.7 %) carry `reason=local_lease_active`:
the local dispatch already returned a `local_lease_active` 503 and the request
re-entered `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` to wait for the protected slot. That
call site passes **no `priority=`**, so the documented "high priority never
queues" contract is not enforced there, and a request that already spent its
queue budget can be handed a fresh 60 s (`LP-0MVV29Y1M004GAW0`).

### 5. The guard admits waits it cannot serve — leading cause hypothesis

For 176 of the 314 abandoned waits a preceding `local_admission_guard`
decision exists in the same session: **170 are `admit`**, median
`projected_wait_s = 35.8 s` (75 of them < 30 s) against an observed 60 s wait.
(Session-level join; own-request correlation is a deliverable of
`LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5`.) The guard prices peer *prefill* service — including the
re-priced occupant remaining new tokens — but not the time a lease holder keeps
the slot while **generating**. This answers open question 1: the shape is a
slot-release modelling gap more than ETA "permissiveness", and it must be
confirmed per-wait before any behaviour change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The abandoned-queue-wait share is restated on a diurnally matched basis (both windows `00:10:18`→`00:10:18` UTC, 24 h, pre-change code ending exactly at the `52085f09` deploy) measured with the same harness revision as the post-change window, and the diurnal-mix contribution is separated from the code-change contribution in a committed record.
- AC2: Queue-wait band attribution is defect-free: no wait is banded by an admission belonging to a different (later or stale) request, a wait with no own-request evidence is reported as `unknown`, and the phantom band (queued waits with zero admission verdicts) is resolved. Unit-tested from synthetic log lines.
- AC3: Queue waits are attributable by entry path (`trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active`) and abandon cause (`cause=queue_wait_expired|queue_depth_exceeded`), logged rather than inferred from duration, reported per trigger/cause, and unit-tested including the pre-change log shape (missing fields degrade to `unknown`).
- AC4: A committed diagnosis record states the cause of the residual (diurnally matched) rise with per-wait evidence: the same-request guard projection vs the observed wait, and the blocker class (prefill in flight vs lease holder generating) that held the slot — explicitly answering whether the guard is too permissive in the ETA sense or blind to the blocker's slot-release time.
- AC5: The `local_lease_active` re-queue path honours the request's priority (`high` never queues there) and charges one queue budget per turn, so cumulative queue wait for a turn cannot exceed `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`; asserted by unit tests.
- AC6: The diagnosed blocker class is priced in the admission guard (or a committed decision records the measured rationale for no change): the guard never admits a queue wait that cannot be served inside the remaining budget because the blocker keeps the slot after its prefill. Rollback uses existing knobs only, the symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor is never lowered, fail-open is preserved, `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) / `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) are unchanged, the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering test stays green, and lease-fairness capping remains owned by `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.
- AC7: A post-fix 24 h window is measured with the same harness and committed; the abandoned share, per-trigger/cause shares and `local_eviction_after_acceptance` classes are compared against the diurnally matched baseline and the literal 85 % bar, with per-hour rates alongside shares.
- AC8: Full test suite green at the pushed commit, and the operator docs (`docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`, the pre/post-change records) carry the restated baseline and the post-fix verdict.

## Plan

Test-first, dependency-ordered slices (each is a vertical slice: code + tests +
docs/record where it applies). Blocked-by edges are wired in Worklog; the
implementing session must run them in this order.

| # | Work item | Scope | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `LP-0MVV29WR0009DY1A` | Fix queue-wait band attribution in the conversion harness (own-request join + carry `new_tokens` on the queue lines; no phantom bands) | — |
| 2 | `LP-0MVV29X2E004INFL` | Attribute queue waits by entry path (`trigger=`) and abandon cause (`cause=`), logged not inferred; harness reports the split | 1 |
| 3 | `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` | Restate the baseline on the diurnally matched 24 h window (52.6 % vs 60.7 %) as a committed record | 1, 2 |
| 4 | `LP-0MVV29XPT003OXI5` | Per-wait diagnosis: same-request guard projection vs observed wait, blocker class, phantom-band proof, +8.1-point attribution | 3 |
| 5 | `LP-0MVV29Y1M004GAW0` | Fix the lease-active re-queue path: pass `priority=`, one queue budget per turn | 2 |
| 6 | `LP-0MVV29YDQ00437N6` | Price the diagnosed blocker class in the guard (or record a no-change decision); no new knob, guardrails unchanged | 4, 5 |
| 7 | `LP-0MVV29YP6006PLNP` | Re-measure the 24 h post-fix share against the diurnal baseline + 85 % bar; update docs/records (runnable deploy+24 h) | 6 |

**Assumptions recorded (see Appendix comment).** (a) The diurnally matched
window is the fair working baseline; the 36.9 % 19:00→19:00 figure is retained
as a historical reference and the parent epic's literal 85 % bar is unchanged.
(b) The 60.7 % total share is taken as correct for the post-change window
(banding does not affect totals) while per-band numbers are treated as
provisional until slice 1 lands. (c) No behaviour change is made before slice 4
produces evidence; slice 6 may legitimately close as a documented no-change
decision. (d) Slice 7 is time-gated on the slice-6 deploy and must stand down
if started early.

data.description:
## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want every queued local wait to record *how it
entered the queue* and *why it left without a slot*, so the abandoned-wait
share can be split by entry path and by cause instead of being a single
opaque 60.7 % — and so a full-budget expiry can never be confused with a
depth-cap refusal.

## Measured need (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Two entry paths feed one queue, and only one of them logs a reason:

| Path | Call site | Abandonments (post-change 24 h) | Logged reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local_concurrency_limit` | `provider.py` first `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call | 89 / 314 (28.3 %) | **none** (the fallback line has no `reason=` field there) |
| `local_lease_active` retry | `provider.py` second `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call, after the local dispatch returned a `local_lease_active` 503 | 225 / 314 (71.7 %) | `reason=local_lease_active` |

Per-window split already derivable from the existing `reason=` field (own
measurement, same harness vocabulary):

| Window (24 h) | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | lease-active share | concurrency-limit share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2026-10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` (pre) | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 41.7 % (20/48) | 23.5 % (4/17) |
| `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `10-29 00:10:18` (pre, diurnal) | 136 | 71 | 52.6 % | 53.3 % (57/107) | 50.0 % (14/28) |
| `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `10-30 00:10:18` (`52085f09`) | 517 | 314 | 60.7 % | 61.1 % (225/368) | 59.7 % (89/149) |

Also measured: **all** abandonments are full-budget expiries
(`queued_duration >= 55 s`; 314/314 post-change, 71/71 pre-change diurnal);
depth-cap refusals (`elapsed ≈ 0`) do not occur, so the 60 s
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` budget is the binding constraint, not
`contention_queue_max_depth`. That distinction is currently *inferred* from
the duration rather than logged.

## Scope

- Log `trigger=concurrency_limit|local_lease_active` on both queue outcomes
  and on the enqueue line, and an explicit `cause=queue_wait_expired|
  queue_depth_exceeded` on both fallback call sites.
- Parse and report the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` in
  `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py` (the existing harness — do NOT
  create a second report; `LP-0MVT110PJ003XYLP` owns the standalone
  contention-queue residual report).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`: add `trigger=` + `cause=` to the two
  `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` and two `contention_queue_dispatch`
  log calls; derive `cause` from the returned action (`elapsed is None` with
  depth at cap → `queue_depth_exceeded`, otherwise `queue_wait_expired`) —
  never guess from the duration in the analyser.
- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`: `_KV_TRIGGER`, `_KV_CAUSE`
  regexes; per-band and totals blocks gain `by_trigger` and `by_cause`
  counters; the markdown record renders the split.
- `tests/test_prefill_admission_conversion.py` + proxy tests: synthetic lines
  for both triggers and both causes; a legacy line without the new fields
  degrades to `unknown`, never dropped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Both fallback call sites log an explicit `cause=` (`queue_wait_expired` vs `queue_depth_exceeded`) and `trigger=` (`concurrency_limit` vs `local_lease_active`); the concurrency-limit site, which currently logs no reason at all, is attributable. Unit-tested from the provider call path.
- AC2: The enqueue line `contention_queue_wait` carries `trigger=` (and keeps `saturation=`), so an enqueue that never resolves is attributable.
- AC3: The harness reports the abandoned share per `trigger` and per `cause` (totals and per band), and a synthetic-line test proves a depth-cap refusal (elapsed ≈ 0, `cause=queue_depth_exceeded`) is distinguished from a budget expiry (`cause=queue_wait_expired`) without inferring from duration.
- AC4: A log line lacking the new fields (pre-change shapes) is parsed as `unknown` and never dropped — asserted by a test using a pre-change line shape.
- AC5: Re-running both committed windows reports the split (expected: 0 depth refusals) with the numbers pasted from tool output, and the record's markdown shows it.
- AC6: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; guardrails `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) / `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120) and the `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` ordering untouched.

## Key Files

- `scripts/prefill_admission_conversion.py`

## Measured finding (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

The fix was deployed at `2026-10-29 00:10:18` UTC (`dev` HEAD `52085f09`), so

24 h window that ends exactly at the deploy — and it is diurnally matched to
the post-change window `2026-10-29 00:10:18` → `2026-10-30 00:10:18`.

Own measurement with the committed harness vocabulary:

| Window (24 h) | Code | Enqueued | Abandoned | Share | Admits | Rejects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `10-27 19:00` → `10-28 19:00` | pre | 65 | 24 | 36.9 % | 423 | 3 954 |

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a per-wait diagnosis of *why* a queue wait
that the admission guard admitted still expires at the 60 s budget — with the
guard's own projection against the observed wait and the class of blocker that
held the slot — so the queue-budget/ETA behaviour can be corrected on measured
evidence rather than on the assumption that "the guard is too permissive".

## Leading hypothesis to test (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Session-level join already measured (post-change window, own analysis):
176 of the 314 abandoned waits have a preceding `local_admission_guard`
decision in the same session; **170 are `admit`** with median
`projected_wait_s = 35.8 s` (75 of them < 30 s) against an observed 60 s wait.

The guard's occupancy term prices the blocker's remaining **prefill**
(`eta_prefill_s * (busy_slots + 1)`, plus the re-priced occupant remaining
service from `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`). It does **not** price the time a lease
holder spends **generating** after its prefill — which is what actually holds
the slot, and which is the shape of 225/314 (71.7 %) abandonments
(`reason=local_lease_active`). If confirmed, the defect is a modelling gap (a
slot-release estimate that ignores decode/lease hold), not ETA optimism.

## Scope

1. A committed analyser, `scripts/queue_wait_diagnosis.py`, emitting one row
   per queue wait: enqueue time, trigger, observed `queued_duration`, cause,
   the guard decision for the **same request** (own-request correlation, not
   session-level), `projected_wait_s` / `eta_occupancy_s` / `busy_slots` /
   `rate_bucket`, and the blocker class at enqueue time (`prefill_in_flight`,
   `lease_holder_generating`, `unknown`) derived from dispatch/lease log
   evidence.
2. A committed diagnosis record under `docs/dev/` answering the parent item's
   open questions with numbers.

This slice is **diagnosis only** — no behaviour change. The fix is the sibling
item that depends on it.

## Minimal implementation

- Reuse `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` for rotation/decompression and the two
  existing harness parsers' field vocabulary; do not add a third log parser.
- Own-request correlation: prefer the request-scoped evidence added by the
  prerequisite children (`contention_queue_wait session= new_tokens=`
  `trigger=`); fall back to (session, nearest preceding admission not already
  consumed by another queue wait) and mark ambiguous rows `ambiguous=true`
  rather than joining them silently.
- Blocker class from `lease_extended_during_prefill` / `dispatch_first_byte_ms`
  / lease release lines in the same window.
- Markdown record produced from the JSON.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `scripts/queue_wait_diagnosis.py --since ... --until ... --json` emits one row per queue wait with enqueue time, trigger, observed wait, cause, the same-request guard projection fields, and blocker class; ambiguous correlations are flagged `ambiguous=true` and never silently joined.
- AC2: Unit tests from synthetic log lines cover: (a) a wait whose same-request admit exists, (b) a wait whose only admission belongs to a different request in the same session (must not be joined, flagged ambiguous), (c) a wait with no admission line at all, (d) blocker classification `prefill_in_flight` vs `lease_holder_generating` vs `unknown`. Deterministic, no live logs, no sleeps.
- AC3: A committed record `docs/dev/queue-wait-abandonment-diagnosis.md` (+ `.json`) answers, with numbers: (a) how many abandoned waits had a same-request admit below budget and how their projected vs observed wait distributes, (b) what held the slot per blocker class and per trigger, (c) where the phantom `32k-64k` waits came from (attribution artefact vs genuine), (d) the diurnal-matched +8.1-point gap split by trigger and blocker class.
- AC4: The record states a clear verdict — modelling gap (decode/lease hold unpriced) vs genuine ETA optimism vs traffic mix — and names at most two candidate behaviour fixes with their expected effect, cross-linking `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` (lease fairness) rather than duplicating it.
- AC5: Every number in the record is pasted from tool output; the embedded command regenerates the JSON.

## Key Files

- `scripts/queue_wait_diagnosis.py` (new), `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` (reuse)
- `docs/dev/queue-wait-abandonment-diagnosis.md` + `.json` (new)
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (read: occupancy term), `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (read: queue call sites)

- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease-fairness fix owner (this item supplies evidence, does not duplicate).
- `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ` — the occupant-remaining re-pricing this diagnosis tests.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the `local_lease_active` re-queue path to
honour the request's priority and to charge a request's queue budget **once per
turn**, so a `high`-priority request is never parked there and a request that
already waited cannot be handed a fresh 60 s.

## Defects found by code reading (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

`proxy/proxy/provider.py` has two `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites:

1. the `local_concurrency_limit` check — passes `priority=_priority`;
2. the `local_lease_active` retry (entered after the local dispatch returned a
   `local_lease_active` 503) — passes **no `priority=`**, so `priority=None`
   reaches both `_contention_queue_enabled(config, priority)` and
   `_prefill_admission_guard(..., priority=priority)`. The documented contract
   is that `high` priority **never queues**; on this path that contract is not
   enforced, and the guard pricing no longer knows the priority either.

Second defect: the lease-active path re-enters the queue **after** the request
already spent its wait (or none) at the concurrency gate, and nothing carries
the spend forward — `_contention_queue_remaining_seconds` is computed for the
*response* but the *next* `wait_for_local_slot` is called with the full
`max_wait_seconds`. A request can therefore accumulate up to two full budgets
in one turn, which inflates both the abandoned-wait denominator and the user's
latency (measured: 368 lease-active waits vs 143 dispatches in the post-change
24 h window, 61.1 % abandoned).

## Scope (bug fix, test-first)

- Pass the priority through on the lease-active call site.
- Carry the spent queue wait on the request and bound the second wait by the
  measured remainder, so cumulative queue wait never exceeds
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` for one turn.
- Keep the guardrails: no new knob, no change to the 60 s / 120 s values.

## Minimal implementation

- `provider.py`: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot(..., priority=_priority)` at the
  lease-active site; read/write the spent-wait marker through the existing
  `_set_queue_wait_on_request` / request attribute used by the deferral path,
  and pass `max_wait_seconds = min(cq_max, remainder)` (a keyword or a new
  helper argument on `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, defaulting to today's
  behaviour for callers that pass nothing).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`: optionally accept an already-spent
  duration so the waiter's own bookkeeping/`queued_duration` reflects the
  cumulative wait (no change to wake-up logic).
- Tests first: high-priority lease-active request does not queue
  (`fallback_policy`-equivalent, no `contention_queue_wait`); a request with a
  spent wait gets at most the remainder; an untouched path behaves
  byte-for-byte as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `local_lease_active` retry call site passes the request's priority, and a unit test asserts a `high`-priority request never waits in that queue (returns without a queue wait, matching the documented `high` never-queues contract).
- AC2: A request that already spent queue wait in the same turn is bounded by the measured remainder at the second wait, and a unit test asserts cumulative queue wait ≤ `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (no second full budget).
- AC3: `queued_duration` / the logged wait for the lease-active path reflects the cumulative wait for the turn (observable), and the `trigger=`/`cause=` fields from the observability sibling are populated on this path.
- AC4: Guardrails unchanged and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering test `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green; no new configuration knob.
- AC5: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing queue, deferral, reservation and lease tests pass unchanged in intent (any intent-preserving update is called out in the commit message).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py` (or the closest existing lease/queue suites)

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: trigger/cause observability.
- `LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C` — the completed item that made the lease denial queue.
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (holder-side capping) — NOT in scope here.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard (or the queue
admit criterion) to price the blocker class the diagnosis proves is holding the
slot — so a queue wait that cannot be served inside the 60 s budget is refused
up-front instead of burning the full budget and detouring remote — or, if the
diagnosis does not support a change, a committed decision that says so.

This is the behaviour-change slice. It is deliberately gated on the diagnosis
record so the change is driven by evidence, not by the assumption that the
guard is "too permissive".

## Context (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Measured in the post-change 24 h window: 314/517 enqueued waits abandoned, all
at the full budget; 225/314 were `reason=local_lease_active`; for the 176
abandonments with a session-level preceding guard decision, 170 were `admit`
with median `projected_wait_s = 35.8 s`. The guard's occupancy term prices peer
*prefill* service (including the re-priced occupant remaining new tokens from
`LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) but not the *generation* time of a lease holder that
keeps the slot after its prefill.

## Scope

- Extend the projected-wait quantity so the diagnosed blocker class is priced
  (for example, a lease/decode hold term raised into the existing occupancy
  maximum — evidence can only raise the floor, never lower it), and/or refuse
  a queue admit whose remaining budget cannot outlast the blocker.
- Preserve every documented invariant: measured evidence can only raise the
  symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor; fail-open on missing/invalid records;
  warm prompts unchanged; no new configuration knob; `high` priority never
  queues.
- Out of scope: capping the lease holder's consecutive renewals — that is
  `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.

## Minimal implementation

- Test first: simulated blockers in `proxy/tests/` — (a) a blocker whose
  remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining budget ⇒ refuse (or
  defer under the pin semantics), (b) a short-prefill blocker ⇒ admit exactly
  as today, (c) missing/invalid occupant record ⇒ fail-open (today's floor).
- Then the minimal guard change in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (plus the
  caller plumbing in `provider.py`/`router_helpers.py` if the blocker snapshot
  is not already available) and the log fields that make the new term
  attributable.
- Document the rollback using existing knobs only
  (`local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A unit test shows a blocker whose remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining queue budget causes a refusal (or the pin-semantics deferral) instead of a full-budget queue wait; a short-prefill blocker still admits with the same decision as today.
- AC2: The change only prices the blocker class named by the diagnosis, never lowers the symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor, and a test asserts fail-open on missing/invalid occupant evidence (no guessed multiplier).
- AC3: Guardrails untouched and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green, no new configuration knob, `high` priority never queues.
- AC4: Rollback is documented using existing knobs only, in `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`, and the page names this item and the diagnosis record as the evidence.
- AC5: The new decision term appears in the `local_admission_guard` log line (parsed by the usage report) so the post-fix window can attribute refusals to it.
- AC6: If the diagnosis does not justify a behaviour change, this item closes with a committed decision note instead of code, recording the measured rationale and re-scoping AC1-AC3 in a comment (no silent no-op).
- AC7: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests pass unchanged in intent.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py`, `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py`
- `docs/dev/contended-prefill-pricing.md`

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: abandoned-wait diagnosis, lease-active re-queue path fixes.
- `LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ` — occupant-remaining re-pricing (the term being extended).
- `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0` — lease fairness (out of scope, linked evidence).
